title: An unramified morphism of algebraic spaces has open diagonal
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be unramified: on compatible representable etale scheme charts it satisfies the scheme property [def-weil-unramified-morphism], using the chart test [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Then the relative diagonal $\Delta_g:X\to X\times_Y X$, with the sheaf fibre product of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], is a representable open immersion. In other words it identifies $X$ with an open subspace $J\subseteq X\times_Y X$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace]; every scheme base change is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. No scheme-representability, separatedness, quasi-compactness or Noetherian hypothesis on $X$ or $Y$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 05W1 (spaces-morphisms-lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), part (1); open immersion and its open image in the subfunctor convention.

proof.text: Put $P=X\times_YX$. Fix any scheme $t:T\to P$, and write $x_1,x_2:T\to X$ for its two components. The sheaf $W=T\times_{P,\Delta_g}X$ is represented by a scheme: on each test scheme it is the equality locus of $x_1$ and $x_2$, hence also the pullback of the representable diagonal $X\to X\times_SX$ along $(x_1,x_2)$. This uses [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The projection $w:W\to T$ is a monomorphism, since a point over $z:C\to T$ must have its $X$ coordinate equal to $x_1z=x_2z$. The equality here is equality of sections on every test scheme, including nonreduced schemes.

source.place: Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), initial representable-monomorphism assertion, expanded using spaces.tex Tag 025Y (definition-algebraic-space).

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $b:V\to Y$, which exists by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By [lem-sfb-unramified-etale-compatible-charts], choose a compatible chart $a:U\to X$, surjective etale, and $h:U\to V$ with $ga=bh$. Unramifiedness of $g$ implies unramifiedness of $h$. Thus $d=\Delta_h:U\to D=U\times_VU$ is an open immersion by [def-weil-unramified-morphism], hence etale by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation].

source.place: Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), choice of U,V and scheme-diagonal input in part (1); morphisms.tex Tags 02GE and 02GP.

proof.text: We check the middle arrow $v:D\to P$ in the source diagram is representable etale. All space fibre products below exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and fibre products of schemes over an algebraic space are schemes by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Put $Q=U\times_YU$ and $R=V\times_YV$. The map $Q\to P$ factors through $X\times_YU$ as two base changes of $a$, so is representable etale by the base-change and composition clauses of the scheme-tests node. The schemes $V,R$ are etale over $Y$: for $R$ use base change and composition of $b$. Its comparison clause therefore makes $\Delta_b:V\to R$ etale. Now $D=Q\times_RV$, where $Q\to R$ sends $(u_1,u_2)$ to $(h(u_1),h(u_2))$: a point of this pullback is $(u_1,u_2,v_0)$ with $h(u_1)=v_0=h(u_2)$; forgetting $v_0$ and inserting its forced value are inverse on all test schemes. Hence $D\to Q$ is etale by base change, and $v:D\to P$ is etale by composition. No surjectivity of $v$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 05W1, cartesian right square and middle vertical arrow; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03EC (lemma-etale-over-space)(2), with representable base change and composition.

proof.text: Let $E=T\times_PD$ and $F=E\times_{D,d}U$. These are schemes, and their maps $E\to T$ and $F\to E$ are etale, by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], using Step 3 and the etaleness of $d$. Thus $F\to T$ is etale by composition. There is a natural identification $F\simeq T\times_{P,\Delta_ga}U\simeq W\times_XU$: the first forgets the $D$ coordinate, which must be $d(u)$; the second inserts the forced $X$ coordinate $a(u)$. Both sides have points $(z,u)$ satisfying $t(z)=(a(u),a(u))$. These operations are inverse and commute with restrictions. Consequently $p:F\to W$ is the base change of the surjective etale $a$, hence surjective etale by the same node. Apply [lem-trf-etale-descent-through-source-cover] to the scheme arrows $F\xrightarrow{p}W\xrightarrow{w}T$. Its hypotheses are now verified, so $w$ is etale.

source.place: Tag 05W1, left square and etale-locality argument in part (1), carried out on an arbitrary scheme test; descent.tex Tag 036W (lemma-etale-etale-local-source).

proof.text: By [def-weil-etale-morphism], etaleness of $w$ gives flatness and local finite presentation. Together with the monomorphism proved in Step 1, these are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-pe-flat-lfp-monomorphism-open], which makes $w$ an open immersion. Since $T\to P$ was arbitrary, $\Delta_g$ is representable by open immersions, with the full scheme structures on all its base changes.

source.place: Tag 025G (theorem-etale-radicial-open), implication (3) implies (1), final input in spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 05W1(1).

proof.text: Define $J$ as the image subfunctor of $\Delta_g$: for a scheme $C$, its sections are the pairs $(x,x)$ with $x\in X(C)$. The map $X\to J$, $x\mapsto(x,x)$, has inverse either projection, naturally in $C$. Thus $J$ is a sheaf isomorphic to $X$. For any $T\to P$, its pullback is the open subscheme $W$ of Step 5. This is exactly the definition of an open subspace in [def-a1-space-open-subspace], so $X\simeq J\subseteq P$ gives the remaining formulation.

source.place: Tag 02YU (definition-immersion), open subspace as an open subfunctor; apply the representable open immersion established in Step 5.

proof_origin.place: Tag 05W1 (lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism), part (1); its etale-locality argument expanded on scheme tests.

lean.statement: theorem diagonal_isRepresentableOpenImmersion_of_unramified {S : Scheme.{u}} {X Y : AlgebraicSpace S} (g : X ⟶ Y) (hg : MapIsLocally (@IsUnramified) g) : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) (pullback.diagonal g.hom).hom ∧ ∃ (hP : IsAlgebraicSpace (Limits.pullback g.hom g.hom)) (J : OpenSubspace ⟨Limits.pullback g.hom g.hom, hP⟩) (e : X.obj.obj ≅ J.val.toFunctor), e.hom ≫ J.val.ι = (pullback.diagonal g.hom).hom
